new_candidates.body:
### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
- LeRobot version: 0.7.1 (main at ff0acf5e; measurements taken at d490e472, src/lerobot/motors unchanged between the two)
- Platform: Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0
- Python version: 3.12.10
- Huggingface Hub version: 1.33.0
- Numpy version: 2.2.6
- PyTorch version: 2.15.0+cpu
- Is PyTorch built with CUDA support?: False
- Using GPU in script?: No
- rustypot 1.13.1
- Robot: SO-101 follower, six STS3215 (model number 777, firmware 3.10), 1 Mbps
```

### Description

While investigating unexpected initial movement on an SO-101 follower, I found that the STS3215 shoulder motor can retain a one-turn position offset after calibration.

The normal reported position can look correct while the extended (multi-turn) position differs by 4096 ticks. Rewriting the homing offset and position limits did not clear this difference. Sending RESET (`0x0A`, not factory reset) cleared it, and so did a power cycle.

Bit 4 of the `Phase` register only chooses whether `Present_Position` shows the multi-turn value; the turn count is kept either way and the position controller uses it. PR #3373 clears that bit in `SerialMotorsBus.configure_motors()`, which hides the reading but not the count, and runs after `calibrate()` in `connect()` anyway.

### Context & Reproduction

### Steps to reproduce

1. SO-101 follower, STS3215 motors, torque off. Write `Homing_Offset` 0 to shoulder_lift (ID 2), as `reset_calibration()` does at the start of a calibration.
2. Move the joint by hand through the encoder's zero (`Present_Position` wraps between 4095 and 0; 4080 → 21 in the records).
3. Run the calibration core: `set_half_turn_homings()`, `record_ranges_of_motion()`, `write_calibration()`. Every register reads back as written and `Present_Position` is inside the recorded range.
4. Read `Present_Position` again with `Phase` bit 4 set (value 28): it is 4096 above the reading with the bit clear (6067 vs 1971 in the records).
5. Enable torque and write a `Goal_Position` a few ticks from the present position: the motor accelerates away with its load rising (2073 → 2039 in 0.22 s, load 56 → 508, until the test's 24-tick stop cut the torque). After a power cycle or RESET (0x0A) the same goal holds.

### How I identified the issue

The starting point was an SO-101 follower whose shoulder moved unexpectedly at the first position command after a calibration that looked correct. It was not the first arm to do so: at least three other SO-101 arms in the same setup had shown the same movement at the first goal after a calibration, the earliest in a record dated 2026-10-17, and the cause had not been identified then. I narrowed the cause in this order, dropping one explanation at a time.

1. **A wrong calibration.** I compared the calibration file with the motor's Home and position limits: they matched. Restoring a known-good calibration to the motor did not remove the movement either.
2. **A wrong goal from the host.** I reviewed the id, sign and angle conversion on the host side and compared the goal I sent with the motor's `Goal_Position` register after the write: they matched. The movement also happened when the new goal equalled the previous one, so it was not the motor returning to an old target.
3. **Internal state depending on power and manual-movement history.** With the same calibration and control code, the motor behaved differently when the pose had been prepared by hand with the power kept on, and when it had been prepared with the power off and then turned on. That pointed at something the motor keeps in RAM across a calibration, rather than at the registers I could read.
4. **The turn count.** Reviewing an STS3215 reimplementation ([0o8o0-blip/sts3215-firmware](https://github.com/0o8o0-blip/sts3215-firmware), a clean-room reimplementation of the STS3215 firmware) showed the position tracked as a turn count plus the wrapped encoder value, with the homing offset applied on top of both. If the real firmware does the same, a joint moved by hand through the wrapped boundary, even by much less than a full revolution, would keep a turn that a later homing offset and position limits do not touch. That is what happens while moving the arm to the middle of its range before `set_half_turn_homings()`, with the homing offset at 0 or stale.
5. **Reproduction on the motor.** With Home at 0 I moved the joint through the boundary, then completed the calibration. The normal position read 1971 and the extended position 6067, exactly 4096 apart. The same run started from the existing Home, without a crossing, showed no difference.

The reimplementation was used to form the hypothesis in step 4 only. Every claim below is a register or wire measurement on a physical STS3215 (shoulder_lift, ID 2), first through raw serial packets with every write read back and every packet journalled, then through `SerialMotorsBus`.

### What I observed

All coordinate and calibration measurements were performed with torque OFF. Powered position-hold comparisons were conducted separately.

First, I set Home to zero and manually moved the shoulder through approximately 105°. The extended position changed from `3197` to `4393`, crossing the 4096-tick boundary. Restoring the original Home value left the extended position at `6165` while the normal position read `2070`. RESET brought the extended position back to `2070`, with the homing offset, limits, Phase, Lock and torque unchanged.

I then compared the first position command under normal and retained-offset conditions:

| Condition | Initial normal / extended position | Goal | Observed position while torque was ON |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Normal reference | 2070 / 2070 | 2069 | Stayed at 2070, load 0 |
| Retained turn offset | 2073 / 6169 | 2069 | Moved from 2073 to 2039 in 0.22 s, load rising from 56 to 508 |
| After RESET | 1996 / 1996 | 1996 | Stayed at 1996 |

With the retained offset, a goal four ticks from the current position had the motor accelerating away with its load rising until the test harness's 24-tick displacement stop cut the torque. The figure is bounded by that stop, not by the motor. Additional movement after torque was disabled is excluded. The post-RESET test was performed at a different starting position.

### Checking the calibration path

I also executed the current LeRobot implementations of:

```text
set_half_turn_homings()
→ record_ranges_of_motion()
→ write_calibration()
```

I compared two initial conditions:

| Initial condition | Normal position after calibration writes | Extended position | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Existing Home applied before movement | 2115 | 2115 | 0 |
| Home 0, boundary crossed before homing | 1971 | 6067 | 4096 |

The second case completed range recording and calibration writes, but the one-turn difference remained.

These measurements used the current calibration methods through a separate serial measurement adapter connected via a virtual serial bridge. They did not exercise the complete LeRobot CLI or rustypot transport path.

Two more checks narrow the cause:

- The same crossing with `Phase` bit 4 clear (value 12) during the move: a 4080 → 21 wrap was observed, and the positions read `2500` normal / `6596` extended after the original Home was written back. The count does not depend on the bit.
- Cutting the 12 V motor power and restoring it cleared the count (`6596` → `2500` with bit 4 set). The count is in RAM, not EEPROM.

Finally, the same calibration core run through `SerialMotorsBus` and rustypot, with the fix proposed below in place, ended with the position at `731` normal and `731` extended after `write_calibration()`, with the registers as written.

### Distinguishing this from other effects

Restoring the original Home and position limits did not resolve the offset, so correct calibration-register values alone were insufficient.

The normal-reference and post-RESET hold tests maintained position during their observation intervals. This differed from the movement observed with the retained turn offset.

Some separate range-test attempts were affected by mechanical interference, communication timeouts, or test-harness stop conditions. I excluded those attempts from the evidence above. A small steady-state tracking error observed in another test was also treated separately from this 4096-tick discrepancy.

### Records

Nothing raised an exception at any point: the calibration-path run completed, the homing offset and position limits read back as written, and the normal reported position was inside the recorded range despite the retained extended-position difference. Earlier powered teleoperation failures did report overload, as described above.

The scripts and the raw records of every run above (packets sent and received, position/torque/Home samples, result files) are on a branch of my fork, one folder per run with an index: https://github.com/Sjeongheon/lerobot/tree/docs/so101-turn-count-records/experiments/so101-turn-count-20261111


### Relevant logs or stack trace

```Shell
# shoulder_lift (ID 2), torque off, Phase 28 (bit 4 set), after the joint was moved by hand through the
# encoder zero and the original Homing_Offset (-1772) and limits (867..3261) were written back.
# Bytes 56-57 of the 87-byte read are Present_Position.
TX ff ff 02 04 02 00 57 a0         READ 87 bytes from address 0
RX ff ff 02 59 00 ... 15 18 ...    Present_Position = 0x1815 = 6165 (2069 + 4096)
TX ff ff 02 02 0a f1               RESET (0x0A)
RX ff ff 02 02 00 fb               status, error 0
TX ff ff 02 04 02 00 57 a0         READ again
RX ff ff 02 59 00 ... 16 08 ...    Present_Position = 0x0816 = 2070; Homing_Offset, limits, Phase, Lock, Torque_Enable unchanged

# first goal with the retained turn: Goal_Position 2069, Present_Position 2073 (bit 4 clear) / 6169 (bit 4 set), torque on
t=0.063 s  present 2073  load  56
t=0.110 s  present 2073  load 152
t=0.141 s  present 2068  load 244
t=0.204 s  present 2059  load 368
t=0.219 s  present 2039  load 508   -> torque cut by the harness's 24-tick stop
# the same goal in a clean state (2070 / 2070) and after RESET (1996 / 1996) held for the whole 0.3 s window
```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [x] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

### Additional Info / Workarounds

### Expected behavior and proposed direction

After calibration is applied, the motor's position reference should be consistent with the calibrated position used for subsequent goals.

The observations suggest clearing the retained turn reference for supported Feetech motors after calibration writes and verification, while torque is OFF. `SerialMotorsBus.write_calibration()` is an appropriate integration point because both newly recorded calibration and reapplication of saved calibration (`_keep_calibration_file`) pass through it. RESET failures should be propagated rather than reporting calibration as successfully completed.

rustypot has no way to send RESET today, so the fix is in two parts:

- rustypot: send the instruction on protocol v1 as `Bus.reset_turn_count(ids)`, with `ServoDefinition.supports_turn_count_reset` true on the STS3215 definition (PR to follow once this issue is up).
- lerobot: `SerialMotorsBus.reset_turn_count()` checks the torque is off and sends it to the motors whose servo has the instruction; `write_calibration()` calls it once every motor's registers are read back as written (PR to follow once this issue is up).

Until the rustypot release lands, cutting the arm's motor power after a calibration clears the count as well. Detecting the count with Phase bit 4 and asking the user to power-cycle would work without rustypot changes, but it leaves the fix to the user, and the auto-calibration path in `connect()` enables the torque in the same call, before anyone could cut the power.

### Related reports, and how this differs

PR #3373 (merged) covers the reading, not the count. The reports below cover the recorded range and the goal clamp, the same crossing seen from other sides. The measurements were repeated over two serial paths, raw packets over pyserial and rustypot, so this is not a transport problem.

- #3586, PR #3589 and PR #5127 (recorded range is wrap-blind): same situation, a joint crossing the encoder's zero during calibration, but a different consequence. Here the recorded range is right and every read sits inside it; what is wrong is a count the host cannot read without setting Phase bit 4. Rejecting wrap jumps during the sweep (#5127) does not cover the crossing while moving the arm to the middle, before `set_half_turn_homings()`, which is where the count forms in the runs above.
- #3585 (a goal outside the limits slams the motor): its Test A, a goal equal to a present position outside the limits moving the motor about 3244 ticks across the seam, is also what a retained turn does; the two can be told apart by reading `Present_Position` with Phase bit 4 set.
- #3587 (choose the homing offset after the sweep): would keep the wrap out of the travel once calibrated, but the count accumulated while moving through the old wrap point before that would still be there; the reset is needed either way.
- PR #3954 (first-frame mismatch guard): compares the action with the observation, and the observation reads correctly here, so it cannot see this state.
new_candidates.title: Feetech STS3215 retains a one-turn position offset after calibration, causing unexpected initial movement
